citation: Vernon-Feagans, L., Kainz, K., Hedrick, A., Ginsberg, M., & Amendum, S. (2013). Live webcam coaching to help early elementary classroom teachers provide effective literacy instruction for struggling readers: The Targeted Reading Intervention. Journal of Educational Psychology, 105(4), 1175-1187. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0032143
report_number: Journal of Educational Psychology, 105(4), 1175-1187; DOI 10.1037/a0032143; ERIC EJ1054424; IES grant R305A040056 (National Research Center for Rural Education Support)
design: Cluster (school-level) RCT. 16 rural schools in 5 poor counties (TX, NM, NE, NC) pair-matched within district on %FRL, size, %minority, Reading First participation; one of each pair randomly assigned to TRI; 1 experimental school withdrew leaving 15 schools (approx 7 intervention + 8 control), 75 K-1 classrooms, 631 children (5 struggling + 5 non-struggling readers randomly selected per classroom). Grades K-1 (registry codes K-2). Subject = Reading/early literacy. Treatment = Targeted Reading Intervention, a classroom-teacher professional development program delivered via biweekly live webcam literacy coaching + 3-day summer workshop; comparison = business-as-usual. Analysis = three-level ANCOVA / hierarchical linear models (students in classrooms in schools), pretest-adjusted, 20 multiply-imputed datasets. Outcomes = 4 WJ-III Diagnostic Reading Battery subtests (Word Attack, Letter Word Identification, Passage Comprehension, Spelling of Sounds) plus PPVT-III vocabulary. Treatment focus = struggling readers (study's primary analytic group).
problems: Single TPD arm (row_id 127) vs business-as-usual; the study's primary student-achievement contrast is SRI vs SRC (struggling readers in intervention vs control schools) -- this is the headline TRI effect. Tests are researcher/developer-administered standardized norm-referenced subtests (WJ-III DRB), best classified as standardized_independent (commercial instrument, not developer-made), though administered/scored as part of the study. Sample sizes per outcome are the spring struggling-reader counts (immediate post = spring of the single treatment year; only one wave). n_clusters=15 schools but per-arm school split not explicitly stated (approx 7 intervention / 8 control after withdrawal). NO ICC reported (Level-3 between-school variance components given but design-effect ICC not reported); never guessed. Impact estimates and SEs come from the 3-level HLM (Table 5 contrasts, SRI vs SRC), so they are cluster-adjusted. g = (contrast b) / sqrt(total model variance L1+L2+L3), J-corrected -- this reproduces the paper's reported effect sizes exactly for WA (.36), LW (.54), PC (.48). EXCEPTION: for Spelling of Sounds the paper reports d=.63 but b=3.23 / sqrt(51.01+2.78+2.63)=3.23/7.51=0.43; the paper's .63 is NOT reproducible from its own stated method (b / sqrt(total variation)) nor from any single variance component -- treated as a likely reporting error and g recomputed as 0.43 from reported b and variance components. PPVT-III is receptive vocabulary (Other, not reading achievement) and is recorded for completeness but flagged is_full_sample=true/outcome_role=secondary; it is not a Reading contrast. No teacher outcomes reported.

effect_sizes.arm_label: TRI (Targeted Reading Intervention) webcam literacy coaching vs business-as-usual; struggling readers (SRI vs SRC)
effect_sizes.test_name: Woodcock-Johnson III Diagnostic Reading Battery - Word Attack
effect_sizes.timepoint: spring (immediate post, end of single treatment year)
effect_sizes.g_method: d = HLM SRI-vs-SRC contrast b (5.66) / sqrt(total model variance = L1 217.69 + L2 16.73 + L3 10.44 = 244.86; sqrt=15.65) = 0.362; J=0.9972 (df=n_t+n_c-2=270); g=0.361. impact_se 2.72 -> se_d=2.72/15.65=0.174 -> g_var=J^2*se_d^2=0.03005. Reproduces paper-reported d=.36 (Table 5).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.1183 Table 5 (Contrasts: SRI vs. SRC, WA = .36); variance components same column
effect_sizes.notes: Word Attack = phonic/structural decoding of nonwords. WJ-III DRB subtest, median reliability .87. b and SE from 3-level pretest-adjusted HLM with 20 multiply-imputed datasets; cluster-adjusted (students in classrooms in schools). n = spring struggling-reader counts (SRI K84+G1 92=176; SRC K51+G1 45=96).
